name: Additional Local or Domain Groups
description:
An adversary may add additional local or domain groups to an adversary-controlled account to maintain persistent access to a system or domain.

On Windows, accounts may use the `net localgroup` and `net group` commands to add existing users to local and domain groups.(Citation: Microsoft Net Localgroup)(Citation: Microsoft Net Group) On Linux, adversaries may use the `usermod` command for the same purpose.(Citation: Linux Usermod)

For example, accounts may be added to the local administrators group on Windows devices to maintain elevated privileges. They may also be added to the Remote Desktop Users group, which allows them to leverage [Remote Desktop Protocol](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001) to log into the endpoints in the future.(Citation: Microsoft RDP Logons) Adversaries may also add accounts to VPN user groups to gain future persistence on the network.(Citation: Cyber Security News) On Linux, accounts may be added to the sudoers group, allowing them to persistently leverage [Sudo and Sudo Caching](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/003) for elevated privileges. 

In Windows environments, machine accounts may also be added to domain groups. This allows the local SYSTEM account to gain privileges on the domain.(Citation: RootDSE AD Detection 2022)

telemetry.name: User Account Modification
telemetry.description: Modification of an account attribute, policy or enabled state.
telemetry.collection_focus: Enable Audit User Account Management and retain the changed attributes and target account; correlate approved administrative requests.

providers.name: Windows Security auditing
providers.scope: Policy-dependent account, object, task and logon records on the host that performs the operation.

providers.name: Active Directory domain controllers
providers.scope: Directory changes and authentication records; collect from the relevant controllers, not only endpoints.

configuration: Use a lab-only GPO under Computer Configuration → Windows Settings → Security Settings → Advanced Audit Policy Configuration. Enable the specific subcategory named below.
For object-level auditing, configure a narrow system access control list (SACL) on the test object in addition to policy. Do not audit an entire production directory by default.

Forward Security events from the responsible host or controller; retain subject and target identities, object identifiers, result and original XML. Confirm effective policy with auditpol /get /category:*.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: A policy checkbox alone does not guarantee an event. Host role, SACL, success/failure selection and audit policy precedence matter. Directory changes may arrive as multiple records.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per principal, host and object: unusual access/request rates, new principal-object relationships, and changes outside approved administration windows. Control for service accounts and scheduled directory maintenance.

strategies.name: Suspicious Addition to Local or Domain Groups

analytics.name: Analytic 0865
analytics.guidance: Detects unauthorized additions of users or machine accounts to privileged local or domain groups (e.g., Administrators, Remote Desktop Users).

tuning.description: Set to detect high-privileged groups like 'Administrators', 'Domain Admins', or 'Remote Desktop Users'
Restrict detections to business hours or approved maintenance windows
Filter out known automated processes or provisioning systems

analytics.name: Analytic 0866
analytics.guidance: Detects unexpected use of usermod, gpasswd, or direct modification of /etc/group to elevate user group membership.

tuning.description: Focus on 'sudo', 'wheel', or custom high-privilege groups
Account that initiated the change (e.g., service account or unrecognized user)

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: SYSCALL for usermod or /etc/group file modification

analytics.name: Analytic 0867
analytics.guidance: Detects use of `dseditgroup` or `dscl` to add users to privileged macOS groups (e.g., admin).

tuning.description: Detect unknown or transient users making group changes
Detect group modifications at suspicious times

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Process execution or directory service changes

software.name: Net
software.description: The `net localgroup` and `net group` commands in [Net](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0039) can be used to add existing users to local and domain groups.(Citation: Microsoft Net Localgroup) (Citation: Microsoft Net Group)

software.name: ServHelper
software.description: [ServHelper](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0382) has added a user named "supportaccount" to the Remote Desktop Users and Administrators groups.(Citation: Proofpoint TA505 Jan 2019)

references.description: Schwarz, D. and Proofpoint Staff. (2019, January 9). ServHelper and FlawedGrace - New malware introduced by TA505. Retrieved May 28, 2019.

software.name: SMOKEDHAM

software.name: DarkGate
software.description: [DarkGate](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1111) elevates accounts created through the malware to the local administration group during execution.(Citation: Ensilo Darkgate 2018)
